subject: SCCs: module sensitivity tiering, recommended modules, and evidence request
messages:
From: Clara Jensen <clara.jensen@novamed.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal EU <legal-eu@novamed.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SCCs — module guidance request and evidence for procurement

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is asking us to confirm which SCC module Redwood intends to adopt for transfers from the EU to the UK/US for the NovaMed integration. Our legal team has a short checklist:

- Which SCC modules will Redwood execute (e.g., Module 2, 3, combination)?
- Any module mapping that affects restricted medical data processing?
- A list of evidence items (SOC 2 report, DPIA summary, encryption attestations) we can attach to our vendor review.

Can you confirm recommended modules given our use case (PHI-adjacent telemetry + de-identified analytics) and share the evidence list and expected timeline to deliver? Procurement would like this by EOB Tuesday.

Appreciate it —
Clara
Senior Procurement Manager
NovaMed Health

---

Note: attached is our vendor intake form (not included).
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Jensen <clara.jensen@novamed.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCCs — module guidance request and evidence for procurement

Thanks Clara — quick summary below. Looping in Legal (Lauren) and Privacy (Vivek) to confirm and to assemble evidence.

Short answer/recommendation:
- Recommended execution: Standard Contractual Clauses (2021) with a Module 2 (UK-specific) + Module 3 fallback pattern for US subprocessors where required. For NovaMed's telemetry (de-identified analytics) plus PHI-adjacent telemetry, we recommend Module 2 as the primary path because the controller-to-processor relationship for EU-origin data is dominant and we will accept Controller-to-Processor obligations under Module 2.
- Rationale: Module 2 provides clearer controller-processor responsibilities and is compatible with our private deployment options and contractual terms. We will include an explicit restriction: no re-identification attempts; telemetry kept at pseudonymized aggregate level.

Evidence we can provide (we'll attach):
- SOC 2 Type II summary (last 12 months) — SOC2-Type2-2026-summary.pdf
- Redwood SCC module decision memo (short) — attached CSV lists modules & mapping
- DPIA summary for analytics pipeline (redacted)
- Data flow diagram highlighting EU exit points and encryption-at-rest/in-transit attestations
- List of subprocessors and country locations; note: US subprocessors are covered by Module 3 fallback where applicable

Timing: Legal can produce the short decision memo and attachable evidence bundle within 48 business hours.

Next steps: Lauren — can you confirm wording we should send to NovaMed's Legal EU team and whether we need to propose an addendum flow (e.g., UK Addendum + DPA clause)? Vivek — please call out any additional DPIA redactions or escalations for PHI-adjacent signals.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Clara Jensen <clara.jensen@novamed.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 12:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCCs — module guidance request and evidence for procurement

Hi all — confirming the recommendation and adding legal nuances.

1) Module selection:
- We will execute the EU Commission SCCs (2021) and accommodate the UK Addendum where NovaMed requires UK-to-third-country crossing specifics. For EU controller data where Redwood acts as processor, Module 2 is appropriate (Controller -> Processor).
- For any subprocessors located in the US processing EU personal data, we will add explicit Module 3 protections as a contractual fallback and include technical controls (encryption in transit + at rest, access controls, logging retention windows).

2) Template language we can offer to NovaMed: brief clause that calls out modules by name and references the SCCs Annex II security commitments. We prefer to avoid bespoke clause-heavy redlines; offer is: execute standard SCCs + Redwood DPA addendum referencing Module 2 primary + Module 3 fallback for US subprocessors.

3) Evidence & procurement pack (we will deliver):
- SOC 2 Type II PDF (redacted where necessary)
- Short DPIA summary (one page)
- Subprocessor list (with country locations)
- SCP/Encryption attestation (one-page)
- SCC module decision memo (one-page)

4) Timeline: we can produce a procurement-ready pack and proposed DPA language by end of day Wednesday (2026-08-26). If NovaMed needs faster, we can provide a preliminary bundle (SOC2 summary + subprocessor list + memo) by COB Tuesday.

5) Operational constraints: we will not accept obligations that create Controller-type warranties beyond those in the SCCs. Also, any request to localize EU data at rest in EU-only data centers will need a Dedicated/Private deployment conversation (separate procurement).

Attaching: SOC2-Type2-2026-summary.pdf and redwood-scc-module-evidence-list.csv (stubs).

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. Procurement will accept the Module 2 + Module 3 fallback approach, and Tuesday preliminary bundle is sufficient to keep us moving.

One quick follow-up from Legal EU: can you confirm whether Redwood's DPIA summary will explicitly call out pseudonymization controls and retention windows for telemetry? If so, please include the retention windows in the preliminary bundle. Also, please confirm who the primary contact for contract redlines will be (we will send the redline to that contact).

If you can get the preliminary bundle by Tuesday morning CET we can slot it in front of our review committee for Wednesday.

Best,
Clara
